name: Agnibaan
note: Suborbital SOrTeD flew 30 May 2024 from own pad ALP-01 Dhanush. No orbital date as of Oct 2026. LEO 100 kg (700 km) in text vs 500 kg in infobox.

name: Alpha
note: List price from secondary sources; returned to flight March 2026

name: Angara-1.2
note: LEO 3.8 t (200 km, 60°); Plesetsk only; military payloads.

name: Angara A5
note: LEO 24.5 t from Plesetsk; GTO 5.4 t Briz-M (7.5 t KVTK); ~US$100m (2021).

name: Antares 330
note: Payload not published on opened page (Antares 230+: ~8,000 kg LEO). Next flight Cygnus NG-22 in 2027 from LP-0A.

name: Ariane 5
note: ESA programme, built by ArianeGroup; last flight July 2023 (117 launches, 112 successes). LEO >20 t (ES), GTO 10,865 kg (ECA).

name: Ariane 6 (62/64)
note: Figures for A64; A62: 10,350 LEO / 7,200 SSO / 4,500 GTO kg. Price est. €100m (A62), €115m (A64), not converted. First A64 Feb 2026.

name: Atlas V
note: 551 variant. Retiring: last flight 2 Jul 2026, six remaining rockets reserved for Starliner. Vandenberg use ended 2022.

name: Aurora-8
note: Operator detail: Reaction Dynamics (RDX). Payload not on opened page (reported 50–200 kg). Maiden orbital flight ~Q3 2028 from Spaceport Nova Scotia (exclusive pad).

name: Blue Whale 1
note: 200 kg to 500 km SSO per SSC 2024 (older sources: 50 kg). No maiden flight found as of Oct 2026.

name: Ceres-1
note: Solid; also sea-launched as Ceres-1S from the Yellow Sea.

name: Ceres-2
note: Maiden flight failed 17 Jan 2026 (GCAT).

name: Chollima-1
note: Operator detail: NATA (North Korea). Capability not public; Wikipedia estimates 200-300 kg LEO (midpoint used). 1/3 successes (Nov 2023 Malligyong-1). No flight since 2023.

name: Daytona
note: Payload not verified. Leases Vandenberg SLC-5; shares Cape SLC-13 allocation (2023) with Vaya Space.

name: Delta IV Heavy
note: Final (16th) flight 9 Apr 2024, NROL-70, SLC-37B.

name: Dnepr
note: Operator detail: Kosmotras (Russia/Ukraine). Converted R-36M ICBM; last orbital launch 2015 (GCAT). Payload not verified, class an estimate.

name: Eclipse (Firefly/Northrop Grumman MLV)
note: Operator detail: Firefly Aerospace / Northrop Grumman. Shares first stage (7 Miranda engines) with Antares 330. First launch targeted 2026 from Wallops, not flown by Oct 2026 (GCAT).

name: Electron
note: Average revenue per launch 2025; the only small launcher in Andøya's market in 2025

name: Epsilon S
note: Second-stage test explosions Jul 2023 and Nov 2024; reverting to older M-35a stage (fired Jul 2026), lowering performance. LOTUSat-1 (Vietnam) contract. First flight FY2026-27.

name: Eris (Block 1)
note: TestFlight 1 (30 Jul 2025) failed after 14 s; TestFlight 2 targeted end-2026. Block 2: up to 1,000 kg LEO.

name: Falcon 9 (Block 5)
note: Expendable figures; reusable 17,500 kg LEO / 5,500 kg GTO (drone ship). Price = 2026 list.

name: Falcon Heavy
note: Fully expended figures; price is reusable configuration (2022). 14 flights, all successful.

name: Falcon 9 (Transporter rideshare)
note: Rideshare service on Falcon 9, not a separate rocket: Rideshare at 7500 USD/kg (2027 list), 50 kg minimum; carried 87% of Andøya's market in 2025

name: Gravity-1 (Yinli-1)
note: Solid, sea-launched; maiden flight Jan 2024.

name: Gravity-2
note: Liquid successor to Gravity-1; listed as future Hainan Commercial user. Payload not verified, class an estimate.

name: GSLV Mk II
note: GTO 2,500 kg is Mk II-specific; LEO/SSO from family infobox. ISRO stopped selling Mk II (Oct 2024); remaining flights for national missions (NISAR Jul 2025).

name: H-IIA
note: Operator detail: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries / JAXA. Retired after F50 (GOSAT-GW) 28 Jun 2025. LEO is low end of 10-15 t family range; GTO 4,100 kg (202) / 6,000 kg (204).

name: H3
note: Operator detail: JAXA / Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. LEO/GTO for H3-24, SSO for H3-30. Price ~JPY 5bn for H3-30. F8 failed Dec 2025 (QZS-5); 3 successes Jun-Oct 2026 incl. MMX.

name: HANBIT-Nano
note: 90 kg to 500 km SSO. First flight 22/23 Dec 2025 from Alcântara failed ~30 s after liftoff; RTF planned Nov 2026.

name: Hyperbola-1
note: Solid; 4 failures in 8 orbital attempts (GCAT).

name: Jielong-3 (Smart Dragon-3)
note: Operator detail: China Rocket Co. (CASC). Solid, sea-launched; SSO 1.6 t (500 km). Class inferred from SSO figure.

name: KAIROS
note: Solid-fuel. LEO 250 kg (500 km, 33 deg), SSO 150 kg (500 km). 0/3 successes (Mar 2024, Dec 2024, Mar 2026).

name: Kinetica-1 (Lijian-1)
note: Solid; LEO 2.0 t, SSO 1.5 t (500 km).

name: Kinetica-2 (Lijian-2)
note: Kerolox, partially reusable design; first flight 30 Mar 2026 (GCAT).

name: Kuaizhou-11
note: Solid; LEO 1.5 t.

name: Kuaizhou-1A
note: Solid, road-mobile; SSO 200 kg (700 km).

name: LauncherOne
note: Air-launched from Boeing 747. Last flight 9 Jan 2023 from Cornwall failed; Virgin Orbit bankrupt 2023. Price was a target (~$12m).

name: Long March 10
note: ~70 t LEO, >=27 t TLI; Mengzhou/Lanyue lunar missions from Wenchang LC-301 (2027+). Reusability not stated.

name: Long March 10A
note: >=18 t LEO expended, >=14 t with recovery; test stage suborbital Feb 2026; orbital debut late 2026/2027.

name: Long March 10B
note: >=16 t LEO (200 km); maiden flight 10 Jul 2026 from Hainan Commercial LC-2 with first-stage recovery.

name: Long March 11
note: Solid; land (mobile) and sea launch.

name: Long March 12
note: First flight Nov 2024 inaugurated Hainan Commercial Spaceport.

name: Long March 12A
note: Operator detail: CASC (SAST). 9 t LEO expended, 6 t with recovery; first flight Dec 2025 reached orbit, landing failed.

name: Long March 12B
note: Operator detail: CASC Commercial Rocket Co.. ~20 t LEO expended, ~12 t reusable; first flight 1 Jun 2026 (Qianfan), no recovery attempt.

name: Long March 2C
note: LEO 3.85 t (200 km), SSO 1.4 t (600 km); flies with YZ-1S upper stage.

name: Long March 2D
note: Workhorse for LEO/SSO from Jiuquan, Taiyuan and Xichang.

name: Long March 2F
note: Crew-rated (Shenzhou); 8.4 t LEO for 2F/G (family table: 8.8 t).

name: Long March 3B/E
note: China's main GTO launcher (BeiDou, comsats); figures for 3B/E.

name: Long March 3C/E
note: GTO 3.9 t; flown from Xichang.

name: Long March 4B
note: SSO 2.8 t per comparison table (family table: 2,295 kg).

name: Long March 4C
note: SSO 2.8 t per comparison table (family table: 2,947 kg).

name: Long March 5
note: GTO 14 t (family table 14.4 t), SSO 15 t (700 km); LEO not stated for base version (5B: 25 t). Lunar/Mars missions.

name: Long March 5B
note: LEO version (station modules, Guowang batches with YZ-2).

name: Long March 6
note: Small kerolox launcher, Taiyuan LC-16.

name: Long March 6A
note: SSO 6.5 t (family table: >5 t); Taiyuan LC-9A, high cadence.

name: Long March 6C
note: SSO 2.4 t (500 km).

name: Long March 7
note: Tianzhou cargo to Tiangong; LEO 13.5 t (family table 14 t); SSO from family table.

name: Long March 7A
note: GTO 7 t (family table 7.8 t).

name: Long March 8
note: SSO 5 t (700 km); originally intended to become partially reusable.

name: Long March 8A
note: LEO >10 t; Qianfan/Guowang batches from Hainan Commercial LC-1.

name: LVM3
note: Operator detail: ISRO / NSIL. First flight 2014 suborbital, first orbital 2017; 9/9 successes to Dec 2025. Commercial: OneWeb, AST BlueBird Block 2 (Dec 2025). Gaganyaan crew vehicle.

name: Maia
note: Operator detail: MaiaSpace (ArianeGroup). 1,500 kg expendable, 500 kg with stage recovery, 2,500 kg with Colibri kick stage. First (orbital) attempt H2 2027 from ex-Soyuz pad.

name: Minotaur IV
note: LEO 200 km at 28.5°; IV+ 1,837 kg. Flew Apr 2025 and Apr 2026 from Vandenberg SLC-8. Price as of 2010.

name: Miura 5
note: First stage recoverable (up to 3 flights). Bases: Kourou, Etlaq Oman (from 2027). First flight slipped from Q1 2026 to later 2026.

name: Nebula-1
note: Reusable kerolox launcher; listed as future Hainan Commercial user. Payload not verified, class an estimate.

name: Neutron
note: Expendable; 13,000 kg with downrange landing. First flight NET 2027 (delay announced Oct 2026). Price per 2023 CNBC report.

name: New Glenn
note: 7×2 config. Three launches (2 successes). May 2026 static-fire explosion destroyed a vehicle and heavily damaged LC-36; price range US$68–110M.

name: New Shepard
note: Suborbital only (up to six passengers or cargo), not an orbital launcher; flights paused from 30 Jan 2026 for at least two years. Launch Site One, Texas.

name: NGLV (Next Generation Launch Vehicle)
note: Future ISRO launcher for the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota (approved Jan 2025). Payload and reusability not taken from an opened source; to verify. Class assumed heavy (ISRO's announced heavy-lift successor to LVM3); payload left empty until sourced.

name: North Korean kerosene/LOX launcher (unnamed)
note: Operator detail: NATA (North Korea). New LOX/petroleum vehicle; debut 27 May 2024 from Sohae failed (first-stage explosion, Malligyong-1-1). Capability unknown. Class assumed small (carried one small reconnaissance satellite).

name: Nuri (KSLV-II)
note: Operator detail: KARI / KASA (Hanwha Aerospace manufacturing). 4/5 successes; flights 4 (Nov 2025) and 5 (Oct 2026) to SSO. Price is a Wikipedia estimate (~USD 30M). 6th launch planned 2027.

name: Orbex Prime
note: Cancelled Feb 2026 when Orbex ceased operations; never flew. Company site gave up to 180 kg SSO. Planned reusable first stage.

name: Pallas-1
note: Kerolox, partially reusable design; first flight 1 Sep 2026 (GCAT).

name: Pegasus XL
note: Air-launched from L-1011. Final flight 3 Jul 2026 from Kwajalein. first_flight = Pegasus family (1990). Price 2017.

name: Proton-M
note: GTO 6.92 t (1800 m/s); ~US$65m; nearing retirement, replaced by Angara A5; one launch since 2024 (Feb 2026).

name: PSLV
note: Operator detail: ISRO / NSIL. PSLV-XL figures. Third-stage failures May 2025 and Jan 2026 (GCAT). Price Rs 130-200 crore (~USD 17-27M). HAL-L&T consortium building 5 PSLV-XL.

name: Qaem 100
note: Solid-fuel; 80 kg to 500 km. Orbital: Mar 2023 fail, Jan 2024 and Sep 2024 successes from Shahroud (site reportedly heavily damaged Mar 2026).

name: RFA One
note: SSO at 500 km. Listed price €3m (unverified, looks low). Maiden flight from SaxaVord slipped after Aug 2026 vehicle issue.

name: Shavit-2
note: Operator detail: Israel Aerospace Industries / Israel Space Agency. LEO 160-300 kg (upper value) into retrograde ~140 deg orbits only. first_flight is Shavit family (1988). Recent: Ofek-16 2020, Ofek-13 2023, Ofek-19 Sep 2025.

name: Simorgh
note: Operator detail: Iranian Space Agency / Ministry of Defence. 250-350 kg to 500 km LEO (low end used). Successes Jan and Dec 2024; Feb 2025 failure reported but not in GCAT. Wikipedia lists retired; pad damaged Mar 2026.

name: Sirius 13
note: Two strap-on boosters version of Sirius family; first commercial flight from ELM-Diamant targeted late 2028.

name: Skyrora XL
note: Three-stage; first flight expected 2027; no orbital licence yet and no assured SaxaVord pad.

name: Space Launch System (Block 1)
note: 27 t to TLI. Price = recurring cost excl. Orion (NASA OIG). Block 1B/2 cancelled Feb 2026. Two flights (Artemis I, II).

name: Soyuz-2.1a
note: Operator detail: Roscosmos (RKTs Progress). LEO 7.02 t from Baikonur, 6.83 t Plesetsk, 7.15 t Vostochny; SSO with Fregat. Crew/cargo to ISS.

name: Soyuz-2.1b
note: Operator detail: Roscosmos (RKTs Progress). SSO/GTO with Fregat; price ~US$35m (2018, Wikipedia Soyuz-2). First-flight year 2006/2008 inconsistent in sources.

name: Soyuz-2.1v
note: Operator detail: Roscosmos (RKTs Progress). 2.85 t LEO (51.8°), 2.8 t from Plesetsk; final flight 5 Feb 2025.

name: Soyuz-5 (Irtysh / Sunkar)
note: Operator detail: Roscosmos (RKTs Progress) with Kazakhstan (Baiterek). Suborbital test 30 Apr 2026 from Baiterek; no orbital flight yet. Other sources say up to 17 t LEO.

name: Soyuz-ST (Soyuz at CSG)
note: Operator detail: Arianespace / Roscosmos. ST-B with Fregat from Kourou (SSO at 820 km). 27 CSG launches 2011–2022; ended after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Soyuz-2 still flies from Russia.

name: Spectrum
note: Price not published; one successful flight of two

name: SSLV
note: Operator detail: ISRO; HAL (after 2025 technology transfer). 2/3 successes, last flight Aug 2024. HAL won ToT (Jun 2025). Expected cost Rs 30-35 crore (~USD 3.1-3.6M). Will move SSO flights to Kulasekarapattinam.

name: Starship / Super Heavy
note: Block 3 figure (Block 1 15 t, Block 2 35 t). 14 flights to Sep 2026; flight 14 deployed first operational payload. Still in test campaign.

name: Nova (Pathfinder)
note: Expendable; 3,000 kg fully reusable. First flight slipped to early 2027 (Sep 2026). Block 2 (2029): 15 t reusable.

name: Terran R
note: Expendable; 23,500 kg with reusable first stage. First flight officially late 2026 (prediction markets lean 2027).

name: Tianlong-3
note: Partially reusable design; maiden flight failed 3 Apr 2026 (GCAT).

name: Tronador II
note: 600 kg to polar orbit (used as SSO figure). First orbital flight target 2030.

name: Tundra
note: 26 m light-lift orbital rocket; payload unpublished. Orbital launches NET 2028 from Atlantic Spaceport Complex. Class assumed small.

name: Vega
note: Operator detail: Arianespace / Avio. LEO figure is 700 km polar; SSO is 400 km. Last flight VV24, 5 Sep 2024 (Sentinel-2C). 22 flights, 2 failures.

name: Vega C
note: 2,300 kg to 700 km SSO; 2,250 kg to 500 km polar. ~€48m (2022). Avio markets it directly since 2026 (SMILE).

name: Vega E
note: Successor of Vega C; maiden flight anticipated 2027. Payload not published; class assumed from the Vega family.

name: Vikram-1
note: India's first private orbital rocket: reached orbit on debut 18 Jul 2026 from SDSC FLP. LEO 350 kg (infobox) vs 480 kg (text). Second test flight before commercial service.

name: Vikram-2
note: Planned 2027 (Wikipedia). Vikram-1U (550 kg LEO) planned Q1 2027.

name: Vulcan Centaur
note: VC6 with upgraded RL10E (base VC6: 14,400 kg GTO). Price is the starting price.

name: Zephyr
note: 19 m two-stage. 2025 plan: first flight from CSG in 2026; later reports point to early 2027 and possibly another site (unverified).

name: ZERO
note: 250 kg to 500 km SSO. To fly from HOSPO LC-1 (completed Oct 2026); first flight planned 2027 (Wikipedia), '2026 at the earliest' per Jiji Dec 2025.

name: Zhuque-2E
note: Methalox; first flight Nov 2024.

name: Zhuque-3
note: 11.8 t expended / 8 t reusable; Zhuque-3E planned 21.3 t. First land booster landing Aug 2026.

name: Zuljanah
note: Operator detail: Iran Ministry of Defence (IRGC per some reports). Two suborbital tests (2021, 2022); 18 Sep 2025 from Semnan failed, possibly first orbital attempt (GCAT counts it as orbital).
